text:
ashwin: FYI - nightly perf runs flagged a regression after the FP8 kernel scheduler change. ~18% p95 token latency increase on seq_len=2048 KV-heavy traces. Short sequences look fine. KV-cache hit rate high (>90%) when problem appears. Posting logs below, thoughts? :thinking:

maria: Can you paste the perf output and which models are affected? opt-family or more broadly? :eyes:

jordan: perf-bot output from last run (summary):
```
model: redwood-open-30b
trace: kv-warmup-2048 (small batch, many prefix hits)
baseline (pre-change): p95 8.2 ms/token, mean 7.1 ms/token
after fp8-sched pr/4123: p95 9.7 ms/token (+18.3%), mean 8.4 ms/token
memory: +0.2% (within noise)
notes: tail gets worse with many small partial KV hits (prefix length variance)
```

ci-bot: Canary deployment for pr/4123 succeeded on canary cluster, but nightly perf detectors flagged the increase and created incident INC-2026-178.

elaine: Hypothesis: kernel selector now favors the FP8 GEMM path for attention when seq > 1024. That FP8 GEMM uses a fused kv-gather that is optimized for full-cache hits but shows worse perf on partial-cache or small-batch cases. We might need to prefer the INT8 attention kernel or use a different KV gather path for FP8 attention.

sanjay: We already exclude embedding and lm_head from quantization in most configs. Confirming we still do that? If yes, quick mitigation is to mark first N attention layers as "sensitive" and force INT8 for them. Proposed minimal config change:
```json
{"quant_policy": "mixed", "exclude_layers": ["embedding", "lm_head", "encoder.layers.0.attn", "encoder.layers.1.attn"]}
```
(This is just the snippet to test)

jordan: Ran a microbench with enforced attention fallback -> results:
```
with fp8-attn (current): p95 9.6 ms/token
with int8-attn (fallback): p95 8.4 ms/token
delta: -12.5% from current, roughly matches nightly regression magnitude
```
so attention FP8 path looks like the culprit on these traces.

ashwin: @maria can you kick off a quick bisect across the scheduler commits (range pr/4100..pr/4130)? If it pins to the scheduler heuristics we should push a hotfix to prefer INT8 for attention by default until we fix the fused KV gather path. :thumbsup:

maria: On it. I'll run per-layer allocation + calibration diffs and a couple of eval prompts to check quality/regression signal. Note: per-layer calibration noise can also affect outputs — we should check eval perplexity before forcing wide fallbacks.

elaine: Also observed small quality jitter when FFN quant scales changed in a prior run — so excluding a handful of sensitive FFN layers may be necessary. Adding a dedicated KV-heavy perf test to nightly should catch this earlier.

sanjay: Agree on adding the KV-heavy nightlies. For immediate rollback: either revert the scheduler change or modify kernel_selector to prefer INT8 for attention when kv_hit_rate < 0.95 or batch_size < 4. Simple policy patch should be quick.

ashwin: OK plan: (1) @maria bisect + calibration check, (2) if confirmed, land policy patch preferring INT8-attn under small-batch/partial-kv conditions, (3) add KV-heavy perf case to nightly, (4) follow up to optimize FP8 fused KV gather.

maria: I'll update this thread with bisect result in ~30m. If urgent, we can roll back scheduler as emergency rollback.

jordan: thanks — also attaching the minimal repro script I used (small-batch, long-prefix random tokens). If anyone wants to repro locally ping me and I can share Docker image.
```bash
# repro outline
python bench_infer.py --model redwood-open-30b --seq 2048 --batch 2 --kv-prefix 1500 --repeat 50
```

ashwin: perfect, thanks everyone. :fire:
